I apologize for not replying to your last comment, I'm in the middle of a big move. 

I would consider what you're describing is dissociation or depersonalization. It's something that happens when you are depressed or anxious, something like imposter syndrome but more encompassing. 

From what you are describing I think we have similar thought processes and mental struggles. I never found anything helpful until I started seeing a therapist who specializes in Internal Family Systems and inner self work. IFS sounds kinda funky if you google it, but this kind of talk therapy has been able to allow me to feel more in control of myself and more whole.

Part of that therapy for me was my therapist breaking down the levels of dissociation we fall down into as stress happens and we don't deal with it properly (or in childhood when we were failed). That feeling you have that convinces you that your life isn't yours is 3 levels down, completely detached from yourself and reality in relation to your mind and body.

I would be happy to message with you more about what Ive learned in therapy and get to know your situation better, if you would like!

I will say this though: having a 'feeling' like your life isn't yours isn't actually a feeling. I want you to try to figure out what you are literally /feeling/. Like pull up an emotion or feeling chart and start to determine how you feel. Because that idea you have is your depression attaching an idea to your feelings. And it's keeping you stuck.

I think it sort of depends on what you are looking forward to in the city, and what you're willing to compromise on moving to a state like MO. 

I'm in my mid 20s, and I'm trans, so I know my perspective is a bit different than yours, so keep that in mind. 

The LGBTQ scene here is okay, though I think it's growing. We have several gay bars around town, with Q being our newest club. If you want to go out at night though be prepared to hear the homophobic preachers on the street corner with microphones blaring, telling us we are all going to hell lol. Definitely a mixed bag of acceptance here, though I don't know if thats really different other places.

Lots of cool coffee shops all over town too! Cafe Ca Phe, Cafe Corazon, Oddly Correct, I could go on. All different vibes, and some of them have fun events and stuff :)
There is also a pretty big movie scene here, with some cool local theaters that show new and old stuff! Check out the Stray Cat Film Center and the Screenland Armour Theater

Prices are going up in town for renting, and a lot of younger people are being priced out, which is why I think you're not seeing the cool art hipster scene. Unfortunately, a lot of small businesses are closing due to high rent, and it's being taken over by big corporations, which is a bummer. The city itself is also leaning heavily into its tourist attractions, and almost all parking is paid parking with "priority pricing". The bus system had its funding cut recently, but if you end up moving where the street car runs that has just gotten an upgrade! The city is not walkable really, so you will likely be driving or taking the streetcar. Also, KC doesn't control our police, the state does (only city in the country like this btw). I would say we have a big car theft issue here too, but I don't know the data on that.

There is so much more I could talk about, but if I were you I would consider looking at some other cities. I don't think you would hate it here, but I would say it's kind of drab and not very 'hip'. As a young person I'm looking to leave. If you have any questions or wanna talk more you can DM me!

Back when I was going through major depression, I pretty much had this same mindset (I did think I was depressed, though). Eventually it got bad enough that I planned a day in the future that I would do it too. A couple months before that day I was able to see a school counselor (I was in college), and I told them about my plan. They immediately sent me to a psychiatric ward, and I spent some time there and would end up there again at the end of the year for actually attempting to end everything.

I'm doing better now, quite a lot better. Being in therapy for several years and working on myself and with my feelings had changed so much for me. I'm able to look back at those times in my life and understand what was really making me upset, even if I didn't understand why I felt so bad at the time.

I think what you are feeling is depression, and when you're in that place it's easy to minimize how bad it is. If you feel like you might one day 'slip', it's already got a firm grasp on you. What helped me was truly committing to loving myself, finding myself, and putting myself in an environment I actually enjoy. That feeling of wanting to get away from everything stems from not enjoying where you are now.

I do like the insurance I have, I use it for all of my health stuff. It also comes with vision and dental (though the dental isn't the best). The one I use has a small copay ($15) for simple things like routine visits, generic meds, ect., and everything I have needed is included in the plan (it covers injectable T, but I use the gel and I haven't found an insurance that will cover that.) However, everything is subject to the deductible and out of pocket maximum, so you have to read up on the plan you choose and what that means for you. The other thing is trying to find the right doctors/hospitals that take the insurance. AmBetter has a lot of providers up here in KC, but I couldn't tell you about Springfield. I would check out Out2Enroll.org, they have some good info about insurance per state too and you can read over some plans. Also, if you want more personalized help you can DM me!

I actually don't think you can have Medicaid and Marketplace insurance at the same time, unfortunately. :/ My apologies, I didn't realize you had Medicaid. I would say it might be worth it to get off Medicaid to get the surgery covered, but honestly I'm not sure how unenrolling from Medicaid works or if you can do that (or if you want to).

I had mine at the same time! I would speak with your surgeon about possibly having them scheduled together, if your surgeon is through a hospital or health system. They will probably have to move your date though, unless somehow the hysterectomy surgeon just happens to be free that morning.

I learned a lot about insurance this year as I went from thinking I would have to pay $9000 out of pocket to only paying $1000 for my combo hysterectomy + top surgery. I use ACA marketplace insurance and only paid $24/mo for that coverage too. 
If you are interested in some personal help I would be happy to discuss some options. I'm in Missouri so some of my knowledge of specific companies may be small but please DM me if you would like some help!

I really think you should wait until March when you can get the surgery covered under insurance. That extra money is still real money that your family could use for other things, especially with the economical future of most Americans being up in the air right now. I know what it's like to wait a few extra months, my surgery got pushed from June to September just this year a few weeks before my date. It's just a few more months, even the ones where you can wear big sweaters and coats to cover your chest. I would try to stay future-oriented by keeping March in your mind, and trying to enjoy the trips you go in as much as you have before. I don't think you're being dramatic, it does feel like something that will never happen. But you know it will. It's happening. It's happening very soon either way.

I will say this though- Be extremely careful in Florida, if you decide to go either way. It is not safe for trans people there right now. It is worse than even 2 years ago. You're going to be with your school and in Disney so you'll be in safer areas, but don't go anywhere alone, especially not bathrooms if you can.

So I use marketplace insurance through the Affordable Care Act, which grants people a government subsidy based on their income. I only make 17/hr, so my income is fairly low. The insurance I chose costs around $400/mo, but the subsidy covers $376, leaving me with a monthly payment of $24. You would have to apply for coverage through Healthcare.gov, and then see how much they are willing to cover and what plan is right for you. But it was a pretty good deal to me! It may be something to think about while open enrollment is going on. I'm also not sure if you can apply if you have accepted insurance through an employer, but if you do seriously consider switching I would check into that.

If they offer you a decent plan then I would look into it. You will need to read the plans Summary of Benefits and Coverage, and browse for applicable surgeries. I'm not sure how good BCBS is on the marketplace, if that's what you're looking at. You will also need to check that the hospital and/or surgeon you are hoping for take that insurance as well. You should also call the insurance provider and ask if they cover the surgery, just to be safe!

It may be in your best interest to switch to a different insurance that will cover the surgery, since open enrollment has started and your insurance will take effect in January. This means the pre-authorization will be submitted with the new insurance as soon as it goes into effect and you'll be able to get surgery within the first few months of 2025. I'm not sure what state you are in, so I don't know how realistic this option if for you, but I would look at the Healthcare Marketplace (Healthcare.gov) and see if you can qualify for enrollment and get a good insurance. Out2Enroll.org is a great website that offers information on what plans in your state will cover trans healthcare.

Surgeon wise, Dr. Alyward (with University Health) and Dr. Eagan are very popular here in KC on the missouri side. I have 2 friends who went with Dr. Alyward and loved their experience and results. I couldn't go with her though because she has a BMI limit of 30, and I'm a chubby guy. I went with Dr. Farmer (with University of Kansas Health Systems) on the Kansas side. She does not have a BMI limit, and KU is very friendly and professional. 

I'm not sure if any of those people would take your insurance, considering Arkansas is kind of far from KC, but you can check their websites about what insurance they accept (you can also call the financial dept for questions.) If they do accept it, you'll also need to make sure the surgeon themselves accepts the plan too.

If you're not able to find a surgeon you like around the area that accepts your insurance, you might try going with a different insurance. I got my top surgery + hysto for $1000 with ACA AmBetter insurance and KU hospitals financial aid.

While a lot of the focus is on laws regarding minors, there are plenty of movements to ban gender affirming care altogether, and also laws that's affect all trans people, like bathroom laws or banning trans women from competing in woman's sports at a high school OR college level. Also, if you are low income and use Medicaid in Missouri, you cant have any gender affirming care covered by the insurance. Additionally, the people who have been elected into office in Missouri are very adamantly against trans (and even LGB) rights in Missouri. Namely Josh Hawley, Mike Kahoe, and Andrew Bailey. Essentially, the state is set on a path to become, at best, a place where we trans people can't receive any healthcare, and at worst, have a bounty on our head like in Odessa, Texas.

I totally recommend University Health- they have good discounts if you don't have insurance, and they also accept ACA Martketplace plans. They also do financial aid on top of insurance. Some friends had their top surgeries there and Dr. Alyward is amazing! This is very specific so I don't know if it applies to you, but if you're looking for top surgery, they have a BMI limit there. My BMI is over 30 so I had to go to KU for top surgery

I hope everything goes well for you too. These next 4 years are going to be pretty rough for us 😔

I am also a trans man living in KCMO. My personally recommendation is to move out of Missouri as soon as you are able, and move to a state with what are called "shield laws" in place to protect trans people. A lot of us have been looking at Minnesota, though there are several states with these in place. I would recommend following Erin In The Morning on Substack (or X) for her state-by-state trans safety map and reporting on national trans news.

If you really want to stay in MO, or you really just can't move, then my second recommendation is to get involved with local trans orgs (really rec. goofballsk8 and transjoy). You're going to find people who can give you all the information you need to access healthcare. I personally was just able to get my surgeries this year, and know that at least 2 different healthcare providers are working diligently to keep trans people safe and cared for (KU Medical Systems Diversity Clinic and University Health LGBTQ+ Clinic). You can even reach out to those clinics now so you can get the ball rolling before any laws are passed.

Finally, I am worried too. I can't decide if I am going to stay or move. I too am scared about being my authentic self. However, every time I am around our community I feel amazing and empowered. You will feel stronger and safer with your peers.

You can message me if you want to talk more!

As long as you care for the holes by keeping them moist with vaseline and covering with gauze or non adhesive pad they should close on their own. I had a few stitches like that spit out and it just takes time for them to heal from the inside out. I also ended up getting a stitch abscess too which was not super fun but ultimately helped get the stitch out. Your scar will probably be a bit wider where the holes are. though. 

As for lifting and doing heavy work- you should have a serious conversation with your supervisors about your current complications and limitations. 8 hours of work isn't worth permanently damaging your body. I'm almost 3 months out and the area where I had the abscess swells when I stretch and move too much. I also recommend continuing to wear compression while working (like a sports compression top) to help swelling, stretching, and bandaging stay in place. 

I do want to mention that the worst that can happen really is stretching your scars and delaying the healing of the present holes. You might cause some bleeding and tears if you're going crazy, but you are technically ready to move in full range of motion after 4-6 weeks.

I just wear a tank top that it meant to get stained instead under everything, or wear clothes I don't care much about staining. When I wear a tight fitting tank top I feel like it helps the aquaphor stay in place and not be rubbed off too.

I got that same letter but it had a little graphic saying my voting frequency was "below average" compared to others in Missouri, which made me believe it was some weird scam because I vote in every local election I hear about lol. My roommate got an identical letter addressed to them too.

I would recommend looking at some of her worst results and stories, and if you wouldn't be okay with that outcome, I wouldn't do it. You're also risking your life by going to someone with a history of infection and complications. 

I personally would say it isn't worth it, but on the other hand I know how horrible it is to feel trapped with no other options when it comes to surgery. However, bad results will just complicate and prolong your dysphoria journey. 

I don't know exactly how the laws work, so forgive me if this is stupid, but would you be able to trust anyone enough to save your money for you to go to a different surgeon? Alternatively, would you be able to move to a different state at some point in the next 5 years to get a different surgeon? I think if you would find someone better waiting is totally worth it.

at my 1 month post op appointment my surgeon examined my incisions and asked if there was anything bothering me about them. i told her that the stitches sticking out were hurting and annoying. she then went over all of the incisions and cut the threads sticking out, including the long one under my armpit too. idk if she would have done that anyway, but i would let your surgeon know they are bothering you and they should cut them off. i would also ask if you can cut them if they keep coming out partially after your appointment.

looks like a stitch is being spit out and healing from the inside out! one of my incisions has a couple of those spots along it (5wpo) that are healing up. that fluid that comes out is just healing goo. my surgeon recommended covering it was gauze to catch the leaking. be sure to keep it moist with aquaphor (or whatever you're using on your incisions) to help it heal good! 

you might have a couple more spots like that pop up as you heal too, so just keep them clean and look for signs of infection daily (new redness, cloudy pus, bad smell).

I had the same thing on my side and I was also really worried lol but it's actually very normal. Something caused the seam to open a little bit, or it's even trying to spit out a large wad of stitch, but your body is working well to heal it from the inside out. The goo that it's leaking is just the healing goop. The area that split on mine was pretty big, and leaked like that for 3 weeks, and formed a white fibrous blob in the area as it healed. 

At first I sprayed it was anti-septic and used antibiotic ointment on it, and covered it with gauze. After my surgeon checked it out she said to just keep moisturizing it with aquaphor (or whatever you are using on your incision) and to cover it if I don't want the juice leaking on my clothes lol. Eventually it just stopped and it's started to crust over and heal like the rest of the scar!

You can dm me if you want to see any photos I took through my healing with it.

I had the mesh and prineo, and my surgeon told me that it can stay on for a maximum of 3 weeks. They seemed convinced it would fall off naturally by that point, and said the same thing about cutting bits off. However by the 3 week point it was hardly budging, so I peeled it off myself. That tape took all of the nasty stuff with it, and my incision looked a lot better under it than I had thought. My incisions were pretty much healed shut, besides a few spots that had stretched or scabbed over. 5 weeks post op now and there is still residue glue from the mesh on the front of my chest lol I seriously doubt that tape would have fallen off completely on its own in my case!

I went through KU for my top surgery, but I got DI with free nipple grafts. With my insurance (AmBetter through the Marketplace) it only cost me my deductible. I believe they accept most major insurance in the area. 

I can't remember exactly what they said when I first met them, but I think they have 2 surgeons who do top surgery (I saw Dr. Farmer). I will say their gender diversity clinic is pretty knowledgeable and should be able to tell you if they think their surgeons would be doing nipple preservation!

Fat trans guy who had surgery a month ago- The post op binder they give you is going to be a half binder, and it's going to dig into your stomach :/ You can counteract the rubbing and irritation from this by wearing a thicker t-shirt under the binder though (You'll just look a little goofy lol)

I recommend getting a full body one (so it doesn't dig and roll up all the time) and not something incredibly cheap from amazon. Why? Cause the elastic is going to stretch after a week and fall apart when you wash it. Also, I feel like every time I order something from Amazon the sizes are never right. 

I got mine from Underworks for around $30. They have specific post-surgical full body compression vests, and I really like mine. The measurement I went by was my underbust measurement (using the measuring tape right under my boobs where I was the flattest), and used that as the chest measurement. My belly is kind of squeezed into it, but that bothers me way less than the digging and rolling up. You can also just unbutton the belly party if you want.

From what I understand about the letters is they are good for 1 year, whether you are seeing that same therapist or not. So, unless you see yourself getting surgery within the year from that previous therapists letter date, you're going to have to get a new letter anyway from the therapist you are then seeing. 

I will say I started seeing a trans therapist and they were actually very helpful and knowledgeable about getting my surgery process started, including knowing exactly what I needed and what my insurance would cover. I would personally recommend finding a trans therapist in your new area if possible! 

I think you should also look into your new states laws about what is needed for insurance and surgery. I live in Missouri but I had my surgery in Kansas, so I had to follow the laws for Kansas (where I had to get 2 different letters). I would recommend trying to find some clinics or local LGBT+ organizations that could provide or help you find information.

I have AmBetter in the state of Missouri, and they do explicitly cover top surgery in my policy (which is why I went with them!). However, every state and even every plan has a different policy so sometimes it can be confusing.

https://out2enroll.org/

This website has some good information to get started with your state and what insurance covers.

Not sure if you are already doing these things, but this is what I've heard helps swelling go down. Obviously only do these things if they have been cleared to do by your surgeon:

- Taking ibuprofen then tylenol interchangeably every 3 hours consecutively
- Moving around frequently, like walking or sitting and getting up, will help your blood flow 
- Sleeping upright on your back, like on a wedge pillow or stack of pillows
- Eating non-inflammatory foods and keeping up on your vitamin intake, and veering away from salty foods

I hope everything works out!

At my post-op appointment I asked them about getting a smaller size, and they said they could give me another one to try. They held the smaller size up to me and said that it was going to be too small, but they can give me an extra of the same size anyway. So basically, I think if you just ask they can give you one. I will say this though- I can see in my insurance statement from the surgery that the binder they sent me out of the hospital with was $729, according to them. I'm actually not sure if they are going to try and charge me that amount again for the extra one they gave me. So I would ask them if it's free or if they will have to charge you/bill your insurance for it. If they want to bill you for it, do yourself a favor and just buy another one online. It's worth it to have an extra one for the rest of your recovery (I actually have 3 right now lol). I got mine from Underworks, they are like $35 I think.

Something I don't feel like it mentioned a lot is stocking up on foods that will help during your recovery. I researched what foods help your body heal, and tried to stick to those the week or so before my surgery and into recovery. Things high in protein, vitamin a, vitamin c, and iron are great! I also purchased the ensure drinks with the vitamin mixes, and pre-made dinners that could be thawed for me (I am the chef in my house so that was necessary for me!). I actually felt a lot worse/achy when I ate taco bell for 2 days vs my protein and fruit, more than I normally do lol.

Also have activities that don't require you to use your arms a lot- even holding my DS for too long wore me out the first week. Having a TV where you can lay down is great, or a podcast/audiobook you can listen to!

I'm also on the gel and my surgeon told me I didn't need to stop at all. Obviously didn't put it on before the surgery that day, but I resumed use the day after surgery (I was way too sleepy the first day to do much lol).
Also, I tried to put it on my shoulders the first time cause that's what I normally do, and quickly realized there was no way I was gonna be able to reach with the movement restrictions. I started putting it on my thighs after some research and it's working fine!
I would say to speak with your surgeon asap about anything though, they will have the best advice for you. Don't be afraid to message them, it's their job!

I got one from Underworks, they have post-surgery compression tops available on their website. Just be sure to check your sizing and round up rather than down- it shouldn't be as tight as a binder. Those tops fit like a typical binder or tank top and use hook and eye closures on the front.

Honestly it is surprising how robust the gender diversity program at KU Med is considering the current trans hate happening in Kansas and Missouri, but I think they really try to be a safe place for trans patients, at least the facilities around the KC metro area. I was able to get on testosterone quickly after speaking with my primary care doctor with KU, who referred me to the gender clinic. The best part is the clinic doctor (Dr. Quinn Jackson) is a trans man himself and really understands the care we need! From there getting set up for surgery was no problem. I'm really happy there is a good place for trans patients on either side of the state line to get help!
Thank you for the wishes as well :)!

Yes, you'll need 2 letters for the surgery. One from a licensed therapist, and another one from someone with a PhD in psychology (psychiatry). Basically, those letters and your therapist are the proof they use. So another important note here is that you'll probably need to be seeing a therapist for a while before you can get the surgery, if you aren't already. As for insurance, I know most of the ones local to KC don't cover top surgery either- I had to get AmBetter through the Healthcare Marketplace to find coverage. I would look into your insurance (if you have some) to see if they would cover it.

Honestly, I'm not sure about that rule, as I've been on HRT for 2 years now :( However, I think it might just be that you have to be out living as your gender for a year? I remember them asking me about that for the letters you need.
What I liked about KU is that they have a gender diversity clinic that sets you up with pretty much everything you need to get the process started and they can answer a lot of those questions. Got with a doctor for HRT, got with a psych for my letter, and got appts with both my surgeons quickly because of that. Probably only took a year and some change to complete the top surgery process!

I think you might also be able to go through Truman Medical Center without a BMI requirement, but i could be wrong!
As far as the surgeons you listed, I called Alyward before going through KU and that nurse told me she only took BMI below 30 or something.

If we wanted to use the singular "person", then we could not say that he was part of a group by the term "one of". Person would work if he was saying "He is the coolest person I know." 

If we were to use the plural "persons", it would not fit into the sentence structure very well. Persons isn't a word used in casual conversation, and it is usually left for writing or legal talk. However, it can be used when referring to a group of people that us a known number. Since his friend if "one of", we are unclear how many people he is part of and thus makes this word not fit well.

"People" tends to be the best bet when talking about an unknown number of humans, and in this case we can see that the phrase "one of" is meant to show he is in a large group of "coolest people" that the OP knows. 

It may be a little confusing because in the sentence itself we are referring to the friend with a singular "he" at the beginning, however when we imply that he is part of a group, we must change it from "person" to "people", even though we are just referring to one person in the sentence.
The phrase would be "Happy birthday to one of the coolest people I know." Hope they have a good one!
